title: Flat scalar extension of derived Hom from a pseudo-coherent complex
statement:
Let $R\to S$ be a flat homomorphism of commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Work in the ordinary derived categories of modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], regarded as sheaves on the one-object site with trivial topology, so $R\operatorname{Hom}$ is [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] and extension of scalars is [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Let $E\in D(R)$ be pseudo-coherent, meaning isomorphic to a bounded-above complex of finite free $R$-modules [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex], and let $L\in D^+(R)$, meaning $H^i(L)=0$ for all sufficiently negative integers $i$. The canonical derived-Hom scalar-extension map
$$R\operatorname{Hom}_R(E,L)\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}S\longrightarrow R\operatorname{Hom}_S(E\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}S,L\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}S)$$
is an isomorphism in $D(S)$, natural in $E$ and $L$. The map is the adjoint, under extension and restriction of scalars, of the map obtained by applying extension of scalars to morphisms and using its unit $L\to L\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}S$. No perfectness of $E$ and no Noetherian hypothesis on either ring is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0A6A (lemma-base-change-RHom), clause (3), including the map of Equation 0E1X and the comparison of Tag 0E1W.

proof.text: Choose $E\simeq Q_RP$ with $P^p=0$ for $p>b$ and all $P^p$ finite free by [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex]. Since $L\in D^+(R)$, choose $L\simeq Q_RN$ with $N^q=0$ for $q<a$ using [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category]. Free modules are projective: lift each basis vector through a surjection and extend linearly. Identify the ordinary and one-object-site module models by [lem-weil-pbc-singleton-site-module-comparison]. Write $F=S\otimes_R-$ termwise. Tensor symmetry $x\otimes s\mapsto s\otimes x$ identifies this with $-\otimes_R S$ and carries the cited unit $x\mapsto x\otimes1$ to $x\mapsto1\otimes x$.

Put $H=\operatorname{Hom}_R^\bullet(P,N)$ and $H\prime=\operatorname{Hom}_S^\bullet(FP,FN)$. Apply [lem-trf-flat-projective-hom-models] to the flat map and bounded-above projective source. Write its model isomorphisms as $e_R:Q_RH\xrightarrow{\sim}R\operatorname{Hom}_R(E,L)$, $c_H:LF(Q_RH)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_SF(H)$, and $B:Q_SH\prime\xrightarrow{\sim}R\operatorname{Hom}_S(LFE,LFL)$. Set $A=c_H\circ LF(e_R^{-1})$. This explicitly gives an isomorphism from $LF(R\operatorname{Hom}_R(E,L))$ to $Q_SF(H)$ even when $H$ is unbounded.

source.place: Tag 0A66 and flat-model refinement of Tag 0A6A(3)

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-half-bounded-hom-scalar-isomorphism] to the representatives and bounds $a,b$ of Step 1. Its normalized chain map $\chi:F(H)\to H'$ is an isomorphism. In degree $n$ only $a-n\le p\le b$ can contribute, including the empty interval, and the finite-support comparison uses $P_{a-n}$ separately in each degree and imposes no perfectness assumption on $E$. Applying the localization functor yields an isomorphism $Q_S\chi$ between the models of Step 2.

Apply [lem-trf-projective-hom-scalar-unit-normalization] to $P,N$. If $\gamma:U R\operatorname{Hom}_S(LFE,LFL)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\operatorname{Hom}_R(E,ULFL)$ is its evaluation-normalized scalar-Hom adjunction, it identifies $B\circ Q_S\chi\circ A$ with the scalar-adjunction transpose of $\gamma^{-1}\circ R\operatorname{Hom}_R(E,\eta_L)$. This is the canonical map in the statement, and is invertible by Steps 2--3. The same cited statement gives naturality in arbitrary derived morphisms and compatibility with representatives, so the result holds for $E,L$ themselves.
